lead_raw_text:
The structure of Ce2Cu6Te8 (CeCu3Te4) crystallizes in the monoclinic space group C2/m (No. 15), with 16 atoms per unit cell distributed over five independent Wyckoff orbits. Geometry-derived analysis shows Cu centers in two environments: an eight-coordinate body-centered-cubic-like local arrangement and a four-coordinate Te-only environment, while Ce is ten-coordinate and Te centers are six- or five-coordinate. Corner-, edge-, and face-sharing are observed among the polyhedra, including corner- and edge-sharing between Cu and Te polyhedra, and the periodic neighbor graph forms a single three-dimensional component.
